objective: Improve the CLI's error handling so that every command surfaces actionable, consistent error messages — distinguishing between expected user errors (no active spec, bad spec ID, unknown agent) and unexpected runtime failures — uses the correct output stream (stderr for errors), and exits with non-zero codes only when appropriate.
outcomes: Every command prints user-facing errors to stderr (console.error) and exits with code 1 on failure — this is already the pattern, but two callsites use console.log for errors instead.
withSpinner shows the error message on spinner.fail() instead of swallowing it silently (currently spinner.fail() shows no text and the raw throw re-surfaces as an unformatted stack if uncaught).
Known user errors (no active spec, spec not found, unknown agent, repo not found, WatsonxConfigError) produce a short, human-readable message with no stack trace.
Unexpected errors (filesystem permission denied, JSON parse failure, network error) include the error class/type so the developer knows it is not a usage mistake.
process.exit(1) is only called at the top-level command boundary, not buried inside shared helpers like selectAgentsOrExit (currently selectAgentsOrExit calls process.exit, making it untestable).
The global unhandled rejection/exception handler in index.ts catches anything that escapes a command and prints it cleanly instead of crashing with a raw Node.js stack trace.

evidence.excerpt: Improve error handling in the CLI
spinner.fail() is called with no message; the raw error is re-thrown and caught by the command's catch block, so the spinner just shows a bare red dot with no text.
selectAgentsOrExit calls process.exit(1) inside a shared helper, making it impossible to unit-test and mixing control-flow concerns with error presentation.
No global uncaughtException or unhandledRejection handler — a command that throws outside its try/catch crashes with a raw Node.js stack trace.
All command catch blocks use err.message directly. If something throws a non-Error (e.g. a plain string), err.message is undefined and the output is 'Failed to ...: undefined'.
Uses console.error(error(...)) consistently — good pattern already established.
Uses console.error(error(...)) and process.exit(1) — the correct pattern.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Spinner fails with the error message shown, then the command's catch block prints the formatted error and exits 1.
Returns null to caller; caller (command) logs the warning and calls process.exit(1) — process.exit is not inside the shared helper.

edgeCases.scenario: Unhandled rejection from a command that forgets try/catch
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Global handler in index.ts catches it, prints formatted error, exits 1.

edgeCases.scenario: Error object has no .message (e.g. a string is thrown)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: formatCommandError falls back to String(err) so no [object Object] output.

edgeCases.scenario: WatsonxConfigError during model init in non-chat commands
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Not applicable — only chat.ts creates the model. Out of scope.

edgeCases.scenario: Spinner is running when process receives SIGINT
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Not changed — SIGINT handling in chat.ts is out of scope; other commands do not intercept SIGINT.

constraints: Do not change any public API or exported types.
chat.ts already has its own well-structured error handling — leave it untouched.
